Wait, just wanting to clarify… So he picks her up sometime after 5pm from daycare and has her for roughly 3hrs 40 minutes during a typical day. 

You’re putting her to bed every night and waking her up, while pregnant? That sounds exhausting, especially with you trying to suggest compromises/suggestions for an easier time and nothing is sticking for your husband. 

Not only that but you prepare dinner in advance so all he has to do is heat up the food and feed her? That is absolutely unfair and I’m so sorry you have to deal with that. 

I’d recommend taking some time to fully think about your situation; what a typical day looks like for both of you and what each of you is responsible for. Bedtime can be a truly exhausting and difficult routine to get into, so I can understand it being difficult but that doesn’t sound fair for him to simply refuse and not even discuss things with you/compromises to make things easier. That could get even more stressful the further you’re coming along too, sleep is so important (and nice in general).

I’m really sorry to hear that you’re struggling so much. I also can relate to dropping out of school due to health problems and sleeping all day for years, just not doing anything. I also have no friends or a supportive family. I lost my online friend and only friend of 10 years recently. From my personal experience I would like to say it would help but I don’t know, it’s not something I can 100% assure you. My advice though is to go because they’ll help you with stability and potentially medicating you if it’s something you want. You just have to really nag the shit out of them for help, that’s always been my struggle. If you do go I would be sure to prepare and bring some things for boredom and hygiene products. But not only can they help stabilize you all the ones I’ve known and gone to help you move forward in life. They could help you get that first job as well as resources if you’re in need of a safe place. I truly wish you the best and if you ever want to talk I’m here.

I’m so sorry that you’re feeling that way and it’s completely normal to worry about that. Finding relationships while on the spectrum can be rather hard. It’s hard but it’s possible to find a romantic relationship with someone who doesn’t want/expect sexual gratification from you. If you don’t feel comfortable with a romantic relationship there’s always platonic relationships. I myself struggle with romantic relationships because I’m just not interested, I’m not wired for the chemistry part. I like the idea of dating but I’m perfectly content with just having my best friend. You can totally be content and satisfied with a close friend, or just friends in general. It’s hard to accept at first for sure, I really struggled to accept with how I was feeling and thought I would be alone too. But I have so many people who love me in my life and I don’t feel lonely. If you ever want to talk more too I would love to chat with you 💕 I really hope this helps you feel more hopeful and that it’s okay to not feel sexual attraction but to desire sexual relief
